summary: We are testing whether a multi-start simulated annealing algorithm with greedy local search can achieve a high score (predicted ≥85/100) on the Max-Cut optimization problem (#192), compared to a naive random assignment baseline (~51/100). This is the first iteration, establishing a strong single-mechanism baseline before exploring more sophisticated approaches.
key_points: Single arm (h-main): Multi-start SA with 20 restarts, greedy + random initialization, greedy local search, and SA cooling schedule (T=3.0→0.001, alpha=0.99997). This approach scored 87.28 in prior probing and is now being formally tested.

Confirmation criterion: Score ≥85 confirms that SA with greedy local search substantially outperforms random assignment and justifies this as a strong baseline. Score <85 would trigger diagnostics — checking for time-limit violations (reduce restarts) or ineffective SA acceptance (verify temperature schedule).

Key risks: (1) The judge may have larger/harder test cases than probing, causing timeouts (n≤1000, m≤20000 with 20 restarts × SA iterations must fit within the time limit). (2) Output format must be exactly one line of space-separated 0/1 values — any deviation scores 0. (3) Fixed seed (42) is used; score variability across judge test cases is the main source of variance.
